research_rationale:
Executive Order 13722 (Blocking Property of the Government of North Korea and the Workers’ Party of Korea, and Prohibiting Certain Transactions With Respect to North Korea; 81 FR 14943) is held in the Federal Register print (FR Doc. 2016-06355) and was read in full. The 36-clause inventory (the opening clause and sections 1 to 13 with their paragraphs) matches the printed text. The order has no sunset or terminating condition of its own. A sentence-by-sentence search of the held texts that print the number 13722 (the Federal Register print, continuation notices, other Federal Register documents and CFR text) for revocation, supersession, rescission, termination, amendment or repeal language next to the number found none. The Federal Register catalog search (later-events:ofr_catalog) returned only cross-references to this order from North Korea notices and related orders. The other general instrument in the packet, Executive Order 14294 of May 9, 2025 (Fighting Overcriminalization in Federal Regulations), does not print this number and states a prosecution policy for criminal regulatory offenses, which gives no reason to treat any clause as extinguished. Executive Order 13722 takes additional steps under the emergency declared in Executive Order 13466, so the held notices continuing that emergency (each from June 2016 on names Executive Order 13722) are the continuation predicate. The later North Korea order held in the packet (Executive Order 13810) recites this order and does not revoke, supersede or amend it. Because the order depends on a declared emergency, the 11 annual continuation notices held for it are attached to every clause; the last, the Notice of June 22, 2026, continues the emergency beyond June 26, 2026, which covers 2026-10-14. Every clause is operative on that date.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No earlier end exists for any clause. The order contains no date, duration, condition or performance trigger that could end a clause. The held later instruments are the 11 annual continuation notices, each of which continues the emergency, and no held instrument revokes, supersedes or amends the order. The Notice of June 22, 2026 itself acts under section 202(d) of the National Emergencies Act (50 U.S.C. 1622(d)) and the emergency rests on IEEPA, so the principal authorities were still operating in 2026; nothing held shows that any authority cited in the order expired or was repealed.","independent_command_check":"The order is a set of continuing commands, prohibitions, findings, definitions, delegations and a reporting authorization. None is a one-time command that was performed and exhausted: entry suspensions apply to an open class and any reporting authorization sets no deadline. No clause is independent of the declared emergency, so one continuing predicate supports all of them. ","savings_check":"Savings were examined in the held text of the order and in the held later instruments. The order contains no savings or transition provision and no held instrument ends it, so no accrued right or transferred function arises.","scope_check":"Each of the 36 clauses was decided separately on the order's own held text, which has no end, read with the 11 held continuation notices and the bounded searches. The packet's current-law leads are sections of the OFAC regulations in 31 CFR (eCFR amended through 2026-11-06) and, where present, U.S. Code sections; their source bytes are not held, so no clause cites them. Definitions, findings and delegations operate only with the blocking command and remain with it. "}
